title.zh: 先排目标，再谈利害：一份铁路议奏的顺序
title.en: Rank the Goals First: A Railway Memorial and the Order of Argument

dek.zh: 台谏请停修京通铁路；张之洞的议奏则排出修路之利的次序、列成条目，并把一条南北线路的北段、南段分给督抚。传文在「得旨報可」之后，接着记他调任湖广，并奏开炼铁厂「資路用」；本传没有记这条线路的修筑经过。
dek.en: The censors asked to halt the Beijing-Tongzhou railway. Zhang Zhidong's memorial ranked the benefits of building railways, set them out as numbered items, and assigned the northern and southern sections of a north-south line to governors-general and a governor. After "approved by rescript," the biography goes on to record his transfer to Huguang and his petition to open an ironworks to supply the railway; this biography does not record how the line itself was built.

paras.zh: 要不要修京通铁路，朝中有了争执。《清史稿·张之洞传》记：「會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」。海军衙门主张修，台谏（负责进言、弹劾的言官）争陈铁路之害、请停办。传文紧接着又记了另外两种主张：「翁同龢等請試修邊地，便用兵；徐會灃請改修德州濟寧路，利漕運」，其后录有本文传主张之洞的议奏。至于台谏所说的害具体是哪几条、海军衙门的理由为何，传文都没有记。
paras.en: The proposed Beijing-Tongzhou railway drew opposition at court. Zhang Zhidong's biography in the Draft History of the Qing records it this way (here and throughout, quotations from the Chinese are our own translations): "When the Naval Office petitioned to build the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, the censors pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted." The Naval Office stood for building; the censors - the court's officials charged with remonstrance and impeachment - pressed the harms and asked for a stop. The biography then records two further proposals: Weng Tonghe and others asked to try building in the frontier regions, for ease of moving troops; Xu Huifeng asked to build a Dezhou-Jining line instead, for the benefit of grain transport. After that it records the memorial of Zhang Zhidong, the subject of this biography. Which harms the censors meant, and what reasons the Naval Office gave, the biography does not record.

paras.zh: 张之洞针对这几种主张上了一份议奏。他的议奏所论是一条以河为界、分南北两段的线路；传文所录未说明它与京通线的关系。议奏中明确排出了目标次序：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之」。目标的轻重被明明白白摆上桌面——作者认为，这个排序是这篇议奏最容易被略过、也最见功夫的地方。
paras.en: Zhang Zhidong answered these proposals with a memorial. The line it discusses is divided by the river into a northern and a southern section; the biography's record does not say how it relates to the Beijing-Tongzhou line. The memorial sets out an explicit ranking of goals: "In building a railway, the greatest benefit lies in moving local goods and enriching the people's livelihood; raising troops and forwarding supplies come second." The relative weight of the goals is laid plainly on the table. In the author's view, that ranking is the easiest thing to skim past in this memorial, and the place where the real craft sits.

heading.en: What He Had Been Up To

paras.zh: 在这之前，张之洞在广东办的是学堂、枪炮厂和矿务局。传文给这几件事安了一个前因：「之洞恥言和，則陰自圖強」，随后「設廣東水陸師學堂，創槍砲廠，開礦務局」。「恥言和」是《清史稿》修撰者写下的动机，并非本文推测。
paras.en: Before this, Zhang had set up an academy, an arsenal, and a mining bureau in Guangdong. The biography gives those ventures a cause: "Ashamed of suing for peace, Zhidong quietly set about making himself strong," and then he founded the Guangdong Naval and Military Academy, created an arsenal, and opened a mining bureau. "Ashamed of suing for peace" is the motive the compilers of the Draft History assigned, not a conjecture of this article.

paras.zh: 到了铁路这桩事上，他给出的目标排序很明确：通土货、厚民生第一，征兵、转饷第二。同一份议奏里，运输物产、改善生计被放在最前，军事用途被放在其次。
paras.en: When it came to the railway, his ranking of goals was explicit: moving local goods and enriching livelihoods first, raising troops and forwarding supplies second. In one and the same memorial, shipping produce and improving the ordinary livelihood sit up front; military use comes after.

paras.zh: 一种解释是，这个排序是有意为之：台谏争的是「鐵路之害」，而翁同龢等已以「便用兵」为由请试修边地；若先论兵事，便与这一主张在同一题目上相争，争执或许更烈（作者推测，传文未载）；把民生摆在前头，等于把辩论引到“土货通不通、民生厚不厚”这类可以逐条说的题目上。作者推断这只是顺序上的策略，传文并未写他这样排的理由。
paras.en: One reading is that the ranking is deliberate. The censors were arguing "the harms of railways," and Weng Tonghe and others had already asked to try building in the frontier regions for ease of moving troops; had he opened on military matters, he would have been contesting the same ground as that proposal, and the fight might have grown hotter (the author's conjecture; the biography does not say so). Placing livelihoods first steers the debate onto ground where points can be settled one by one - do local goods flow, do livelihoods thicken. The author infers this is tactics in the ordering; the biography records no reason of his own for the sequence.

heading.en: Turning the Arguments into a List

paras.zh: 议奏逐条列「利」，传文留下了编号：利一到利七，每条一两句，最后一条是「海上用兵，漕運無梗，利七」；议奏随即提出「有此七利，分段分年成之」。这组「利」是他自己列举的理由，不是独立核算过的数字。
paras.en: The memorial works through a numbered list of benefits, and the biography preserves the numbering: benefit one through benefit seven, each a sentence or two. The last reads: "Should war come by sea, grain transport will not be obstructed - benefit seven." The memorial then proposes: "With these seven benefits, let it be completed section by section, year by year." These are reasons he assembled himself, not figures from any independent accounting.

paras.zh: 前两条很朴素：「內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二」。利一讲路在腹地、不至于引敌，利二讲原野开阔、坟墓与房屋容易避开。一种解释是，它们针对的是安全与迁坟拆屋的顾虑，但传文未记台谏所指何害。作者认为，值得记住的正是这半句：在一个「務宏大」的人笔下，最具体的落点是沿线的坟墓与房屋能不能绕开。
paras.en: The first two are plain: "Situated in the interior, there is no fear of drawing in the enemy - benefit one; the open plains are broad, and graves and houses can easily be avoided - benefit two." Benefit one says the line lies in the interior and will not draw in an enemy; benefit two says the country is open, so graves and dwellings can easily be routed around. One reading is that they address worries about security and about moved graves and demolished homes, but the biography does not record which harms the censors meant. In the author's view, worth remembering is precisely that half-sentence: under the pen of a man the verdict calls "grand in scale," the most concrete landing point is whether the graves and houses along the route can be spared.

paras.zh: 第三、四条转向生计与饷源：「廠盛站多，役夫賈客可舍舊圖新，利三；以一路控八九省之衢，人貨輻輳，足裕餉源，利四」。车站和工厂多起来，做工的人、跑买卖的人可以另谋出路；一条路控住八九省的要冲，人与货聚拢，饷源也就有了着落。作者认为，利三与「厚民生」相呼应；利四则落在饷源上。
paras.en: Benefits three and four turn to livelihoods and revenue: "As works flourish and stations multiply, laborers and traders can leave the old for the new - benefit three; with one route commanding the crossroads of eight or nine provinces, people and goods converge, and the sources of military pay are made ample - benefit four." Hired hands and traveling merchants can find new lines of work; one line holds the crossroads of eight or nine provinces, people and goods crowd in, and revenue has somewhere to come from. In the author's view, benefit three echoes "enriching the people's livelihood"; benefit four lands on the sources of military pay.

paras.zh: 第五条讲集兵，第六条讲煤铁开采：「近畿有事，淮、楚精兵崇朝可集，利五；太原旺煤鐵，運行便則開採必多，利六」。京畿一带有事，淮、楚精兵一早便可集结；太原煤铁旺盛，运输方便则开采必多。
paras.en: Benefit five concerns gathering troops, benefit six coal and iron mining: "Should trouble arise near the capital, the picked troops of Huai and Chu can be gathered within a single morning - benefit five; Taiyuan is rich in coal and iron, and where transport is easy, mining will certainly increase - benefit six." If trouble arises in the region around the capital, the picked troops of Huai and Chu can assemble within a morning; Taiyuan is rich in coal and iron, and easier transport means more mining.

paras.zh: 接着是接续图景。北路一段，「河北路成，則三晉之轍接於井陘，關隴之驂交於洛口」——山西的车辙接上井陉，关陇的车马交于洛口。南路一段，「自河以南，則東引淮、吳，南通湘、蜀，萬里聲息，刻期可通」。他没有停在一条线上，而是把议奏中的线路画成以河为界的南北两段、各自接上更大路网的样子。
paras.en: Then comes the picture of connections. Of the northern stretch: "When the northern line is complete, the wheel-ruts of the Three Jin will meet at Jingxing, and the teams of Guan and Long will cross at Luokou" - Shanxi's cart-tracks connect at Jingxing, and the horse-teams of Guan and Long meet at Luokou. Of the southern stretch: "South of the river it will draw in Huai and Wu to the east and reach Xiang and Shu in the south; news from ten thousand li away can be carried on schedule." He does not stop at one line; he draws the line in his memorial as two stretches, north and south of the river, each hooking into a larger network.

paras.zh: 再往下是分工：「北路責之直隸總督，南路責之湖廣總督，副以河南巡撫」。北路归直隶总督，南路归湖广总督，河南巡抚做副手。谁扛哪一段，写得清清楚楚；作者认为，这样没有留下各段无人专责的余地。
paras.en: Then the division of labor: "Let the northern section be the charge of the Governor-General of Zhili, and the southern section the charge of the Governor-General of Huguang, assisted by the Governor of Henan." Who carries which stretch is written out plainly. In the author's view, this leaves no room for a section that no one is specifically responsible for.

paras.zh: 结果是「得旨報可，遂有移楚之命」。朝廷准了这份奏请，随后有调他赴湖广之命。需要说清楚的是，「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工；张之洞本传没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁，只在其后记他奏开炼铁厂「資路用」；同卷《王文韶传》记有京汉铁路兴筑，是否即此线，本文不作断定，也不替他补写这些细节。
paras.en: The outcome: "The memorial received an approving rescript, and there followed the order transferring him to Huguang." The throne approved the request, and an order sending him to Huguang followed. Be clear: "approved by rescript" means the memorial was accepted, not that work began. Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the line he proposed; it goes on only to record his petition for an ironworks to supply the railway. The biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter records the building of the Beijing-Hankou railway; whether that is this line, this article does not decide, and it will not supply the missing details.

paras.zh: 到湖广之后，传文记的是另一串兴作：大冶产铁、江西萍乡产煤，他奏请在汉阳大别山下开炼铁厂，资路用，同时设枪炮钢药专厂；又因荆襄宜桑棉麻枲而饶皮革，设织布、纺纱、缫丝、制麻革诸局；再以堤工相佐、币政相通，「由是湖北財賦稱饒，土木工作亦日興矣」。铁路之外，铁厂、厂局、堤工、币政被串成一串。
paras.en: At Huguang the biography records another string of undertakings. Daye yielded iron and Pingxiang in Jiangxi yielded coal, so he petitioned to open an ironworks below Mount Dabie at Hanyang to supply the railway, and at the same time specialist works for rifles, cannon, steel, and powder. Because Jing and Xiang grew mulberry, cotton, hemp, and ramie and had hides to spare, he set up bureaus for weaving cloth, spinning yarn, reeling silk, and making hemp and leather. He backed them with dike works and knit them together with currency measures: "From this Hubei's revenues came to be called abundant, and building works rose by the day." Beyond the railway, ironworks, bureaus, dikes, and currency were strung into one chain.

paras.zh: 传文对他有一句评语：「蒞官所至，必有興作。務宏大，不問費多寡」。传文同时记他任疆寄数十年，「及卒，家不增一畝」。一种解释是，这句话与前面那份编号清单出自同一种风格——敢开大摊子，也肯把摊子一条条写出来；至于花费，评语说他不问多寡，传文并未举出具体用款数字；按「家不增一畝」这一限定，“不问花费”不宜读作为私谋利。
paras.en: The biography passes a verdict on him: "Wherever he took office, he had works begun. He aimed at the grand, and did not ask how much it cost." It also records that after decades as a provincial official, "at his death, his family had not gained a single mu of land." One reading: that verdict and the numbered list share the same style - bold enough to open big undertakings, willing to write each out item by item. As for spending, the verdict says he did not ask the amount; the biography gives no figures. Read with the qualifier about his family's land, "did not ask how much it cost" should not be taken as spending for private gain.

paras.zh: 作者的一种读法是，这份议奏至少包含以下四个部分（另有南北接续的图景）：排目标次序（通土货、厚民生最大，征兵转饷次之），列逐条的「利」并编号（共七条），提出「分段分年成之」，落实到官职（北路直隶总督、南路湖广总督、河南巡抚为副）。作者认为，这样写可能把争论从“有没有害”引向“这些逐条的「利」成不成立、这三位督抚之职扛不扛得动”。
paras.en: One reading is that the memorial includes at least four components (besides the picture of connections): a ranking of goals (moving goods and enriching livelihoods greatest, raising troops and forwarding supplies next); a numbered, item-by-item list of benefits, seven in all; a proposal to complete the line section by section, year by year; and responsibility assigned to offices (north to the Governor-General of Zhili, south to the Governor-General of Huguang, the Governor of Henan as deputy). In the author's view, writing it this way may steer the argument away from "is it harmful" toward "do these itemized benefits hold, and can these three offices carry them."

paras.zh: 一种解释是，「厚民生」排在「徵兵、轉餉」之前，是把争议最小、也最难被驳倒的目标放在最前面：台谏说的是「鐵路之害」，而不至引敌、坟庐易避这两条或许是对着「害」字去答的（传文未记台谏所指何害）。作者推断这种写法出于策略考虑，传文没有写他的思考过程，此处是作者的解释。
paras.en: One reading: putting "enriching livelihoods" before "raising troops and forwarding supplies" sets the least contested, hardest-to-topple goal at the front. The censors spoke of "the harms of railways," and the two points about not drawing in the enemy and easily avoiding graves and houses may answer the word "harms," though the biography does not record which harms were meant. The author infers that this drafting is tactical; the biography records no thought process, so this is the author's interpretation.

paras.zh: 作者提出的替代选择（传文所录议奏中未见，属反事实）：议奏已主张「分段分年成之」，但传文所录议奏中没有先试修一小段、看运量与扰民程度再定其余各段的设计；传文记翁同龢等曾「請試修邊地」，但那是为「便用兵」，不是先修一段、以运量和扰民程度决定其余各段。另一种做法是把「利」逐条配上可核对的口径，让反对者逐条检验，这在传文所录议奏中也未见。这两种设计是作者提出的比较项，不是传文所录议奏里的内容。
paras.en: Alternatives the author offers (not found in the memorial as the biography records it, therefore counterfactual): the memorial already proposes completing the line section by section, year by year, but the recorded text has no design for building a short stretch first and letting freight volumes and the degree of disruption decide the rest. The biography does record that Weng Tonghe and others asked to try building in the frontier regions, but that was for ease of moving troops, not a matter of building one stretch first and letting freight volumes and disruption decide the remaining sections. Another option would be to attach a checkable yardstick to each "benefit," so opponents could test them one by one, and that too does not appear in the memorial as recorded. Both designs are comparison items the author raises, not part of the memorial as the biography records it.

paras.zh: 写一份提案或评审材料时，可以借用这份议奏的顺序：开头不急着罗列优劣，先交代哪个目标最重、哪个其次，把轻重写在最前面；随后把支持的理由分条编号，像那七条编号的“利”一样，每一条都留给读者去追问“成不成立”。
paras.en: When drafting a proposal or a review document, you can borrow this memorial's order: rather than opening with a list of pros and cons, state up front which goal weighs most and which comes next; then number the supporting reasons one by one, like those seven numbered benefits, leaving each open to the reader's challenge: "does this hold?"

paras.zh: 方案定下来之后，第二步是分几步做、谁负责哪一段：北路归谁、南路归谁、谁做副手，写清楚，不留模糊地带。同时说好第一段什么时候可以单独验收，让一段先跑起来，而不是等全线贯通才第一次检验。
paras.en: Once the plan is chosen, the second step is stages and owners: who takes the northern stretch, who the southern, who serves as deputy - written down, no fuzzy territory. At the same time agree when the first stage can be checked on its own, so a stretch gets running and tested early rather than waiting for the whole line to be joined before the first inspection.

heading.zh: 这份材料没能告诉我们的
heading.en: What This Source Cannot Tell Us

paras.zh: 首先，本文主要依据《清史稿·张之洞传》，另引同卷《王文韶传》一条线索，未用《清史稿》以外的记载对照。台谏所说的「鐵路之害」是哪几条、海军衙门的理由为何，传文一概未录，所以本文只能写到「爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」为止。
paras.en: First, this article relies mainly on Zhang Zhidong's biography in the Draft History of the Qing, plus one lead from the biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter, and has not checked it against any record outside the Draft History. Which harms the censors meant, and what reasons the Naval Office gave, the biography records not at all; so this article can go no further than "pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted."

paras.zh: 其次，那段议奏文字是史书所录的文字，未必是他逐字说过的话；本文所引文字均按史书所录转述。那组「利」是他自己列举的理由，不是独立核算过的数字，不能当作成本收益分析来读。
paras.en: Second, the memorial text is documentary text as the historians recorded it, not necessarily words he spoke verbatim; all text quoted in this article is reported as the history records it. That set of "benefits" is a list of reasons he compiled himself, not independently audited figures, and cannot be read as cost-benefit analysis.

paras.zh: 再次，张之洞本传没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁，只在其后记他奏开炼铁厂「資路用」；同卷《王文韶传》有京汉铁路兴筑的记载，是否同一线路无法确定，本文不替他补写；「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工，更不等于办成。本文也不把原文没有的公元年份换算出来，更不会说他事先知道结果——他写下那些「利」的时候，看到的只是清单，不是成绩单。
paras.en: Third, Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the proposed line; it goes on only to record his petition for an ironworks to supply the railway. The biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter records the building of the Beijing-Hankou railway, but whether it is the same line cannot be determined, and this article does not fill in the gaps. "Approved by rescript" is approval, not the start of work, still less a finished line. This article also converts no Common Era years the original does not have, and will not say he knew the outcome in advance: when he wrote those numbered benefits, what lay before him was a checklist, not a report card.

reflection.type: 不确定下决策的判断问题

scenario.zh: 一个十来人的小组要决定是否把用了多年的旧系统整体重写：一方主张推倒重来，一方主张小修小补，还有人主张今年干脆不动，三边都拿不出压倒对方的数据。
scenario.en: A team of ten or so must decide whether to rewrite an old system they have run for years: one side wants to tear it down and start over, one wants incremental patching, one says leave it alone this year - and none of the three can produce data that overpowers the others.

question.zh: 在没有第二种独立核算、也没有人能保证结果的情况下，你会怎么把目标的优先级公开排出来，并把每一方的理由改写成可以逐条检验的清单？如果让你把这件事拆成几步、分给具体的人，你先砍掉哪一步，为什么？
question.en: With no second independent audit available and nobody able to guarantee the outcome, how would you publish the ranking of priorities, and rewrite each side's reasons as a checklist that can be tested point by point? If you had to break the work into stages and assign them to named people, which stage would you cut first, and why?

assumptions.zh:
各方分歧主要在目标的轻重，而不是事实真假
短期内拿不到第三方核算数据
团队里至少有一个人愿意为每一段的验收负责
assumptions.en: The disagreement is mainly about the weight of goals, not about what is true; third-party audit data will not arrive in the short term; at least one person on the team is willing to be accountable for the acceptance of each stage.

steps.zh:
先定目标排序：把“对用户最要紧的是什么”排在第一位，把“技术上最漂亮”排在其次，并公开写出这个顺序
把三种主张各写成编号清单：每条一句，注明依据是什么、怎么算成立、怎么算被推翻
按清单选方案后，把工作拆成两三段，每段写明负责人和一段就能验收的成果
约定第一段做完就回头对照清单，成不成立当场看
steps.en: First fix and publish the goal ranking: put "what matters most to users" first and "what is technically prettiest" second, in writing and up front. Next write each of the three positions as a numbered checklist: one line per item, stating the basis, what counts as holding, and what would refute it. Then choose by the checklist, split the work into two or three stages, and name the owner and a checkable result for each stage. Finally agree that when the first stage is done you return to the checklist and see on the spot which items hold.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：不做全量决定，先用两周做一小段试点，拿真实数据再定整体方案；也可以保留旧系统只换最要紧的一段。这两种做法在本案记录里都没有出现，是作者提出的比较项。
alternative.en: The author's alternative: decide nothing wholesale; run a two-week pilot on one small stretch and use real data to settle the whole plan - or keep the old system and replace only the part that matters most. Neither appears in this case record; both are comparison items the author raises.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文主要据《清史稿·张之洞传》，另引同卷《王文韶传》一条，无《清史稿》以外的记载对照；议奏文字按史书所录转述，未必是逐字原话；「利」为他自列的理由，非独立核算；张之洞本传未记工期、用款、拆迁，同卷《王文韶传》所记京汉铁路兴筑是否即此线，未作断定；「得旨報可」仅为准奏，不等于开工；不换算公元年份，亦不假定他事先知道结果。
uncertainty_note.en: This article rests mainly on one source, the biography of Zhang Zhidong in the Draft History of the Qing, plus one lead from the biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter, with no record outside the Draft History for comparison. The memorial text is reported as the historians recorded it and may not be verbatim; the "benefits" are reasons he listed himself, not independent figures; Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations, and whether the Beijing-Hankou railway recorded in the biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter is this line is left undecided; "approved by rescript" means approval only, not the start of work. No Common Era years are converted, and no foreknowledge of the outcome is assumed.

preheader.zh: 该不该修、修哪条：先排出目标次序，再把七条利弊写成可以逐条反驳的清单
preheader.en: Build it at all, and where? He ranked the goals first, then wrote seven checkable reasons instead of arguing by volume.
